short: Twenty-one years of war that moved Baltic supremacy from Sweden to Russia.
full:
Denmark, Saxony-Poland and Russia formed a coalition against the seventeen-year-old Charles XII and moved in February 1700, Augustus the Strong marching on Riga while the Danes invaded Holstein-Gottorp. Charles knocked Denmark out of the war by August, relieved Narva in November, and then turned on Poland instead of Russia - the decision that gave Peter I the years he needed to rebuild his army and to found St Petersburg on captured Ingrian ground in 1703.

The Swedish invasion of Russia launched in 1708 ended at Poltava in July 1709, followed by the surrender of the remaining army at Perevolochna three days later. The coalition immediately re-formed, joined later by Prussia and Hanover, and Sweden spent another twelve years losing its German and Baltic provinces piecemeal while its king was first in Ottoman exile and then campaigning in Norway. Peace came with Denmark and Hanover in 1719 and 1720 and with Russia at Nystad in 1721, which left Russia a Baltic power and a European one.
